sourcedFrom: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c (2022)
cleanIntro: The PDP PRO SD is a PDP: Walther's own download area lists the PDP pistols book against it, under both the Compact and the Full Size entries, and that book is the one this guide follows. It strips like every PDP — trigger press, take-down catch, slide off the front — and the book then publishes a genuine deeper procedure for the striker, the extractor and the magazine. The extractor half of that splits by slide type, so read your slide before you pick up a punch.

steps.title: Establish which PDP frame and which slide you have
steps.action: The PDP book prints two specification tables, PDP Compact and PDP Full Size, and the PRO SD is listed under both — so check the frame first: the Compact grip carries a 15-round magazine, the Full Size an 18-round one. Then look at the top of the slide: a cover plate or a reflex sight mount base means an OR model, a plain slide means an open-sight model.
steps.prose: The book is written for the PDP family and never prints the words PRO SD, so the two questions it does ask are the ones you answer here. Compact and Full Size differ by grip height and magazine capacity, not by anything you touch during a field strip, but the magazines are not interchangeable and Walther is explicit that a magazine may enter another model's well and still not function in it. The slide question is the one that changes what you do later: OR and open-sight slides release their extractors by opposite motions. A threaded-barrel PDP is 15 mm longer in barrel and overall length than the table figure.
steps.caution: Walther's own caution: a magazine will only function properly in the specific model it was designed for, and swapping between models can cause a malfunction or damage the pistol and magazine.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 6 Technical Specifications, PDP Compact table, printed p.27 (PDF p.29); the PDP Full Size table follows on printed p.28 (PDF p.30)

steps.title: Magazine out of the well, finger outside the guard
steps.action: Finger straight along the frame and outside the trigger guard, muzzle in a safe direction, press the reversible magazine release and pull the magazine clear of the well.
steps.prose: A loaded PDP magazine can drop straight out and land on its feed lips, which is exactly the kind of damage that produces feeding trouble later — catch it. Put it out of arm's reach of the bench before you go any further, because this procedure ends in a trigger press. The witness holes on the tube tell you at a glance how many rounds you have just set aside, so use them; that number is what you compare against once the pistol is stripped.
steps.quote: Grasp the pistol with your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard. Depress the magazine release and remove the magazine from the pistol (2.3.2 Figure 1).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 2.3.2 Magazine Release, printed p.9 (PDF p.11)

steps.title: Slide back, locked open, and check the bore while you are there
steps.action: Draw the slide fully rearward in one brisk stroke from the rear serrations, let it ease forward a fraction while pressing up on the slide stop to lock it open, then verify the chamber is unloaded and check the bore is clean, dry and free of obstructions.
steps.prose: The bore check is not padding — a bore with oil or preservative standing in it raises pressure when it is fired, and with the slide locked back you can see straight through from the breech. Do not obstruct the ejection port with the supporting hand while you rack; a blocked port can drop a chambered round back into the action rather than clearing it. Look down the magazine well too, so the frame is confirmed as well as the chamber.
steps.quote: Check the chamber to verify that it is unloaded and check the bore visually that it is clean, dry, and free from any obstructions (3.1 Figure 4).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 3.1 Inspecting the Pistol, printed p.10 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: The colour mark on the extractor proves nothing
steps.action: Do not use the loaded chamber indicator as your clear check. The extractor's colour marking is an indicator, not a verification — confirm the empty chamber visually with the slide locked open.
steps.prose: On the PDP the extractor doubles as the loaded chamber indicator, showing a colour mark when a cartridge or a fired case is in the chamber. That puts the indicator in the dirtiest part of the slide, where it gets scrubbed every time you clean the gun, so it is least reliable on a pistol that is about to be stripped. Read the chamber, not the paint.
steps.quote: The extractor doubles as a loaded chamber indicator. A color marking is visible when a cartridge or fired case is in the chamber (2.3.1 Fig. 1).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 2.3.1 Loaded Chamber Indicator, printed p.8 (PDF p.10)
steps.warn: If you do not see the red dot, do not assume the chamber is empty.

steps.title: Slide down gently, then the mandatory trigger press
steps.action: Pull the slide slightly rearward off the stop and release it slowly so it runs forward under control. Point the muzzle in a safe direction and squeeze the trigger fully to the rear to release the striker.
steps.prose: The PDP's take-down catch cannot be depressed with the striker cocked, so this press is a required part of the strip rather than an optional habit. Everything that has gone before exists to make this press safe, so take one more look into the chamber and the magazine well immediately before your finger moves. Letting the slide run home slowly rather than dropping it saves the extractor a needless impact on a bare chamber.
steps.quote: Close the slide: Pull the slide slightly to the rear. Slowly release the slide, allowing it to return to forward position.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.17)
steps.warn: To complete disassembly you will be required to pull the trigger. A live round left in the chamber will discharge at this step.

steps.title: Take-down catch down on both sides, slide off the front
steps.action: Grip the take-down catch from above with thumb and forefinger, one on each side, and press it straight down. Hold it there and run the slide forward off the frame rails.
steps.prose: Squeezing only one side cants the catch in its slot and it will simply refuse — this is where most people conclude the gun is stuck when they have loaded it unevenly. Working from above rather than from in front keeps the hand behind the muzzle. Once the catch is clear the slide comes off the front with little resistance, so support it. Take the whole slide assembly off in one movement rather than easing it forward in stages.
steps.quote: Move the slide forward, and remove it from the frame.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.17)

steps.title: Recoil assembly out against its spring, then the barrel
steps.action: Invert the slide, lift the recoil guide rod assembly out from beneath the barrel while taking up the spring pressure, then lift the barrel free of the slide.
steps.prose: The recoil assembly is still under load even though it is captive, and its large polymer end sits in a recess under the barrel — pull rather than ease and it will jump out of your hand. Take the pressure on a thumb, roll the rear end out of the recess, and it comes away without drama. The barrel then lifts straight out. You should now be looking at four parts and nothing else.
steps.aside: Flex in the recoil guide rod assembly when it is reinstalled is normal and expected — Walther says so in the reassembly note. It is not a bent rod.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.17)

steps.title: OR or open sight — and never cycle an OR slide bare
steps.action: With the slide off, identify it. A PDP OR model carries a cover plate or a reflex sight mount base secured by two T10 screws; a PDP Open Sight model has neither. If you take that plate or base off, do not operate or hand-cycle the pistol until it is back on.
steps.prose: The plate or base caps the extractor pin channel on an OR slide, and Walther warns that running the gun without it can throw the extractor pin and the extractor out of the slide. It also decides which of two extractor procedures applies to you: the book heads one section PDP OR Models and the next PDP Open Sight Models, and they move the extractor pin in opposite directions. If you are dismounting an optic to clean under it, refit the plate or base before the slide is cycled even once, and do not mix its metric M3x6 screws with the screws supplied with a sight.
steps.quote: Operating the gun without cover plate or mount base may cause the extractor pin and the extractor to fly out.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.3 Extractor, note, printed p.17 (PDF p.19)
steps.warn: Do not read across between the two extractor procedures. PDP OR Models drift the pin OUT; PDP Open Sight Models force it IN against a spring.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Four components: frame, slide, barrel, recoil guide rod assembly. That is the whole published field strip for the PDP — striker, extractor and magazine belong to the deeper procedure.
steps.prose: Lay them out and compare against the main-components figure before any solvent is opened. The routine clean from here reaches the bore, the chamber end, the breech face, the extractor and its surroundings, and the frame — everything a range session actually fouls. The striker channel is deliberately outside that list because it does not get lubricated; if it needs attention, that is the deep procedure and it needs a 2 mm drift punch.
steps.quote: The main components of the pistol are shown in 4.1.1 Figure 3.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.17)

deepSteps.title: Drift the end cap off the back of the slide
deepSteps.action: Stand the slide on its muzzle on a smooth flat surface and hold it by the rear serrations. Push the pin in through the square opening at the top right of the slide end cap with a 2 mm drift punch, and with it held in, slide the end cap downwards out of the slide.
deepSteps.prose: The end cap is holding back the striker spring, so it wants to leave the moment the pin releases it — a thumb across the cap turns a launch into a controlled slide. Standing the slide on its muzzle keeps everything falling towards you instead of across the bench. The opening is square and offset to the right of the cap; use an actual 2 mm punch, because the hole is sized for it and a substitute will chew the edges.
deepSteps.quote: Place the muzzle end of the slide on a smooth, flat surface. Grasp the slide at the rear slide serrations, push in the pin through the square opening located at the top right side of the slide end cap using a 2 mm drift punch (4.2.1 Fig. 1) and remove the slide end cap by sliding it downwards (4.2.1 Fig. 2).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.2.1 Remove Striker Assembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.18)
deepSteps.warn: The striker assembly behind that cap is spring-loaded. Control it as the cap clears the slide.

deepSteps.title: Striker assembly out, and treat it as one part
deepSteps.action: Withdraw the striker assembly rearward out of the slide and set it down noting which way up it sat.
deepSteps.prose: It leaves the slide as a single unit and Walther publishes no further breakdown of it, so clean it as a unit — this is a degreasing job, not a rebuild. Note its orientation now rather than working it out later with a spring under a thumb. Wipe it dry and leave it dry; the reason for opening a PDP slide is to get oil out of this area.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the striker assembly from the slide (4.2.1 Fig. 3).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.2.1 Remove Striker Assembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.18)

deepSteps.title: The striker blocks the striker safety — order is not optional
deepSteps.action: If the striker safety is coming out, remove the striker assembly first, then continue with the extractor and the striker safety. Never try to lift the safety with the striker still in the slide.
deepSteps.prose: The striker physically interferes with the striker safety, so the safety cannot rise while the striker is home, and forcing it damages the plunger rather than freeing it. Once the striker is gone the safety plunger has somewhere to move and the extractor will pivot without a fight. Even if all you wanted was to clean a gummed extractor, the striker still comes out first.
deepSteps.quote: The striker interferes with the striker safety. If you want to remove the striker safety, first remove the striker assembly as described in section 4.2, and then continue with the extractor and the striker safety.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.3 Extractor, note, printed p.17 (PDF p.19)

deepSteps.title: PDP OR Models: cover plate off, extractor pin drifted OUT
deepSteps.action: On an optics-ready slide, take off the cover plate or the reflex sight and its mount base first. Then hold the slide upside down and drift the extractor pin straight out with a 2 mm punch, keeping a finger over the striker safety as it comes.
deepSteps.prose: The OR slide's extractor pin passes clean through and simply exits; there is no spring resisting it, which is why this procedure looks nothing like the open-sight one. Your finger over the striker safety is the only thing retaining it once the pin is gone, so put it there before the punch moves. Pivot the extractor's rear end out slowly rather than levering it against the slide, then lift the striker safety assembly out and keep it with the extractor.
deepSteps.quote: Hold the slide upside down. Use a 2 mm drift punch to drift the extractor pin out (4.3.1 Fig. 1).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.3.1 Remove Extractor — PDP OR Models, printed p.17 (PDF p.19)

deepSteps.title: PDP Open Sight Models: extractor pin forced IN against the spring
deepSteps.action: On an open-sight slide, lay the slide upside down with the muzzle to the left and drive the extractor pin INTO the slide against its spring until the rear end of the pin pops proud. Take the punch away, cover the striker safety and the extractor plunger with a finger, then pivot the extractor out.
deepSteps.prose: This is the reverse motion to the OR slide and the reason mixing the two procedures goes badly: here the pin is spring-loaded, so pushing it the way an OR pin goes only compresses the spring and burrs the pin end. When the rear end stands proud, withdraw the punch and pick the pin out. Two sprung parts are then loose under your finger — the striker safety and the extractor plunger — and both will leave the slide if you lift it, so remove them deliberately and lay them out in order.
deepSteps.quote: Cover the striker safety and the extractor plunger with a finger while you pivot the extractor out. Remove the striker safety assembly and the extractor plunger assembly from the slide (4.3.1 Fig. 2)
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.3.1 Remove Extractor — PDP Open Sight Models, printed p.18 (PDF p.20)

deepSteps.title: The extractor spring stays in its slot
deepSteps.action: Leave the extractor spring seated inside the extractor slot. Clean around it and do not prise it out.
deepSteps.prose: One end of that spring is a larger-diameter coil, and that oversize coil is what keeps it captive in the slot. Pull it and you have a fiddly refit ahead with a real chance of installing it the wrong way round, which changes extractor tension. Flood the slot with solvent on a brush, work it, and let it drain instead.
deepSteps.quote: Do not remove the extractor spring from its seat inside the extractor slot. The extractor spring has on one side an end coil of larger diameter which secures it from falling out.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.3.1 Remove Extractor, printed p.17 (PDF p.19)

deepSteps.title: Magazine down to its parts
deepSteps.action: Depress the floorplate catch through the hole in the floorplate with a 4 mm drift punch, slide the floorplate forward off the tube while keeping the catch pressed, then remove the catch and spring out through the bottom and turn the tube upright to release the follower.
deepSteps.prose: The floorplate catch is all that restrains a long, strong spring — keep a thumb over the floorplate as it slides forward or the catch will go across the room. If yours is a +2 magazine the release is different: locate the metal tab at the rear base, and with the floorplate fully seated rearward push that tab upward with a flat-bladed screwdriver until it stands out from the base, then slide the floorplate as usual. Note which way the follower sits before it drops out.
deepSteps.quote: Using a 4 mm drift punch, depress the floorplate catch through the hole in the floorplate (4.4.1. Figure 1).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.4.1 Magazine Disassembly, printed p.20 (PDF p.22)
deepSteps.warn: The magazine spring is under pressure. Control the floorplate catch and the spring while the floorplate comes off.

deepSteps.title: Striker channel dry, and only drops everywhere else
deepSteps.action: Degrease the striker channel and the striker assembly and leave both dry. Put no gun lubricant into the striker channel. Everywhere else, one drop at a time.
deepSteps.prose: Oil in a striker channel picks up powder and carbon and sets into a paste that slows the striker — the symptom is a light primer strike that reads as bad ammunition and is not. The slide's ration: one drop on the safety plunger, one in the disconnector cut. The frame takes one on each slide guide and one on the trigger bar; the barrel, a wiped film outside and on the ramp where the locking block cams it.
deepSteps.caution: Do not put any gun lubricant into the striker channel. Excess lubricant anywhere attracts dirt, unburned powder and carbon residue.
deepSteps.quote: Frame: Put only one drop of lubricant on the slide guides (C), and on the trigger bar (D).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP PISTOLS — Rev.c — 4.6 Lubrication, printed p.22 (PDF p.24)

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Brush from the CHAMBER end through to the muzzle until the bristles fully exit, then pull straight back until they fully exit the chamber end — never reverse direction with the brush in the bore
Powder-removing solvent and a brass bristle bore brush to lift lead and firing residue out of the bore
Wipe out with patches or a swab, then a light film of gun lubricant on the barrel's external surfaces and on the ramp where the locking block cams it
Before firing, wipe all excess oil and preservative out of the bore and chamber

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & EXTRACTOR
tasks: Small brush in solvent around the breech face, the chamber end of the barrel, the extractor and everything nearby that has seen powder or primer residue
Clean around the extractor without lifting its spring out of the slot
One drop of lubricant on the safety plunger, one in the disconnector cut — nothing more in the slide
Striker channel DRY: no lubricant at any point
OR models: refit the cover plate or mount base and secure both M3x6 screws before the slide is cycled — around 2 Nm, with the base pulled toward its front stop while tightening

cleaning.name: FRAME & RAILS
tasks: Light brushing with solvent to remove residue from the frame
One drop of lubricant on each slide guide, one on the trigger bar
Light film of high quality gun lubricant on all external metal surfaces, then wipe clean
In a cold climate use a lubricant that will not congeal at low temperature

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Light film of gun lubricant on the magazine's external metal surfaces only
Wipe the tube interior dry — oil inside the tube collects grit and drags the follower
Inspect feed lips and follower while the magazine is apart, and never force parts back together
+2 magazines: hold the metal tab flush with the body while sliding the floorplate fully rearward, then push the tab back into its seat

cleaning.name: SOLVENT LIMITS
tasks: Do not use ammonia-based or strong alkaline solvents on any Walther firearm
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning; 50 °C (122 °F) is the ultrasonic ceiling
Use only products developed for firearms maintenance — some cleaners damage the pistol's finish

reassembly: Slide upside down, barrel in with the locking lugs oriented as the manual's figure shows.

Smaller black end of the recoil rod into the spring mounting at the front of the slide, then the large polymer end of the recoil spring into the lower barrel recess while taking up the spring pressure. Some flex as it seats is normal.
Push the slide onto the frame from the front until the take-down catch engages, making sure the slide has also picked up the REAR slide guides — front rails only feels right and is not.
Release the slide and let it run fully forward into the locked position.
OR models: cover plate or reflex mount base back on, both M3x6 screws to about 2 Nm with the base held toward its front stop, and check the accessory is firmly seated before firing.
Magazine: follower, spring and floorplate catch back in exactly their original orientation, floorplate slid on until the catch's round projection snaps audibly into its hole.
Dry-patch the bore and wipe the chamber before the pistol is loaded or carried.
fncheck: Magazine out and chamber confirmed empty: rack the slide and let it go — it must run fully into battery on its own. Lock it back on the slide stop and release with the thumb; it should drop and lock up without a nudge. Insert an empty magazine and tug down on the exposed floorplate; it must not move. With the striker cocked, try the take-down catch — it should not go down. Press the trigger and it should. Check the extractor sits flush and returns when pressed. On an OR slide, confirm the cover plate or mount base is fitted and its screws are tight before the pistol goes back into service.
